q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a lead-acid battery?
title: Lead-acid battery carbon footprint
short: Lead is most of the total. Multiply lead and alloy per battery by your supplier's factor, where recycled secondary lead is far lower than primary. Add the plastic case, separators, acid, grid casting and formation electricity. Divide by batteries passed, and report each Ah rating separately.

ul: Lead and lead alloy for grids and oxide: ask your smelter for a per-tonne figure and its recycled share.
Lead melting pots and grid casting: PNG, LPG or electricity.
Formation charging: a large electricity draw, often the biggest plant line.

p: Report per battery for each Ah rating, and per kWh of capacity if a buyer compares chemistries. End-of-life recycling is a separate stage, not a deduction.

example.title: Worked example: battery plant per unit (one month)
lines: Melting PNG: 15,000 SCM x 2.05 = 30,750 kg CO2
Plant total: 243,750 / 40,000 = 6.09 kg CO2 per battery
Add lead, plastic, separators and acid for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
